newsitem.title: CANADA: Canada has room to cut UI premiums - minister.
newsitem.headline: Canada has room to cut UI premiums - minister.

text.p: Canada's newly re-elected Liberal government has "quite a lot of room" to reduce unemployment insurance premiums, Industry Minister John Manley said on Wednesday.

"If the demand on the (employment insurance) fund continues to decrease, there's quite a lot of room for reduction of EI premiums, because the surplus that's being generated is quite large," Manley told Reuters in a telephone interview from Montreal.
Manley was the industry minister in the Liberals' first term and said he hoped to continue in that role. The Liberals were re-elected on Monday with a slim majority.
The surplus in the employment insurance fund was C$5.5 billion at the end of 1996 and government officials expect that to more than double by the end of 1997.
During the election campaign, the Liberals came under pressure to devote the surplus to creating jobs and reducing premiums.

The premiums for employees stand at C$2.90 per C$100 of insurable earnings and the Liberals have pledged to reduce the rate to C$2.80 per C$100 in 1998. Employers pay a set 1.4 times the amount employees pay.
Manley would not say how much more the government would be willing to reduce the premiums. The matter would be dealt with in the autumn, he said.
But he added that some of the reductions in unemployment insurance premiums would be offset by higher contributions to the Canada Pension Plan.
